opportunities.title: Cronos Halted Its Own Chain After a $75M Exploit — That's Not Decentralization, That's a Kill Switch
opportunities.why_now: Cronos froze the network after the Tectonic exploit, exposing the admin-key reality behind 'decentralized' L1s.
opportunities.angle: Security teardown: walk through what 'halting a chain' actually requires (validator coordination, multisig authority) and why that centralization is the real story, not the exploit itself.

opportunities.title: $114M in 48 Hours: Lazarus, More Markets, and Tectonic Are the Same Story Wearing Different Masks
opportunities.why_now: Three unrelated-looking incidents (Lazarus $30M through Hyperliquid, More Markets $9.3M drain, Cronos/Tectonic $75M) hit within 48 hours, all traceable to the same category of failure: unaudited reserve logic and lax bridge/oracle controls.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition roundup — a single chart/timeline post showing the total weekly hack tally and the recurring root causes, closing with 'you already know how this ends' framing.

opportunities.title: Lazarus Just Used Hyperliquid Like a Bank — Perp DEXs Are the New Laundering Rail
opportunities.why_now: On-chain sleuths tied $30M in Lazarus-linked funds moving through Hyperliquid, showing state-sponsored actors now treat high-liquidity DEXs as exit liquidity.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/thread on how sanctioned actors exploit permissionless perp venues for laundering, and what that means for Hyperliquid's growing TradFi partnerships (tie to Hyperliquid Strategies' $2.5B facility news).

opportunities.title: OpenAI's Astra Can Build Attacks Without a Human — Crypto's Smart Contract Audits Just Got a Countdown Clock
opportunities.why_now: OpenAI disclosed Astra can autonomously construct attacks, a direct threat multiplier for an industry that just lost $114M+ to human-built exploits in one week.
opportunities.angle: Forward-looking security op-ed: if AI can now automate exploit discovery, audit firms and bug bounty timelines are already obsolete — what protocols need to change now.

opportunities.title: Tether Froze $42.4M Before the Warrant Existed — 'Not Your Keys' Was Never About Hackers
opportunities.why_now: A new lawsuit alleges Tether froze funds months before any U.S. warrant was issued, reviving the custody-risk argument right as institutions pile into stablecoin ventures (Citi/Goldman) and RWA rails.
opportunities.angle: Security-led custody piece: frame stablecoin issuer discretion as the same risk category as exchange hacks — funds you don't control, seized without due process, dressed up as compliance.
